summary: Connection-level idle batching fanout causing intermittent p95/p99 timeouts under falling QPS
description: Issue summary: Since weekend deploy (canary v2026-03-08) StellarApps started seeing repeated p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s on generation endpoints. Impact: Several customer endpoints saw aggregated p99 jump from ~120ms to 1.8-2.2s for short periods (5-10 minutes) resulting in user-facing timeouts and retries. Environment: Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-32), prod us-east primary; steady QPS 6-10 rps per model but observed during traffic drops (2-3 rps) behavior worsens. Suspected area: continuous-batching behavior when connections go idle then re-awaken, causing many connections to fall into a single coalescing window and creating large head-of-line batches that exceed latency SLOs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On dedicated pool customer-dedicated-32, deploy a load generator that ramps QPS from 8 rps to 2 rps over 2 minutes and holds for 10 minutes.
2) Observe per-connection session re-use (keepalive) and watch continuous-batcher metrics in /metrics (batch_size, batch_wait_ms, queue_depth).
3) Send requests with variable input lengths (avg 256 tokens) to force KV cache warm paths.
4) Repeat a few times; p95/p99 spikes should reproduce within 1-3 minutes of ramp down/up transitions.

investigation_notes: Support replicated with customer on a staging-like dedicated pool; latency spikes align with periods where multiple keepalive connections rejoin after idle and are grouped into one large batch by continuous-batcher.
Hypothesis A: batcher idle timeout and fanout logic is overly permissive after deploy change (v2026-03-08) causing large coalesced windows under low QPS.
Hypothesis B: KV cache cold/warm transitions amplify per-token compute at tail, making large batches exceed SLOs causing upstream timeouts.
Observed batch_size distribution: heavy tail with >40 requests in single batch during incidents; prior baseline had median batch size 6-8.
Checked autoscaling events: no GPU shortage/fallbacks reported. No related 5xx from node-level OOMs.
Tentative correlation to commit 9f3b7c4 which changed idle detection thresholds and introduced connection affinity optimization.

Anya Ruiz (Eng - Serving Runtime) 2026-03-12: Noted recent change in PR github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4321 that touched idle batching heuristics. Will test reverting that flag in a canary.
Priya Nair (Support) 2026-03-13: Customer accepted temporary workaround (reduce keepalive to 15s and enable per-connection jitter). Monitoring for regressions.
Ethan Cole (SRE) 2026-03-13: Added temporary gating to limit max_batch_size to 24 for affected pool. Early telemetry shows p99 back down to ~220ms during prior spike windows.
resolution: Workaround applied: limited max_batch_size to 24 on customer-dedicated-32 and reduced keepalive window at API gateway. Engineering to revert/patch idle-detection change from PR 4321 and introduce per-connection jitter + adaptive fanout cap. Plan: deploy hotfix v2026-03-14 with tests and rollout to remaining dedicated pools.
notes_for_followup: 1) Engineering to add regression test that simulates QPS ramp-down/up and verifies batch_size distribution remains bounded.
2) Post-deployment monitoring: increased sampling for continuous-batcher metrics + alert threshold when median_wait > 120ms for >2m.
3) Customer follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC to review root cause and timelines.
